title: Constructibility descends through surjective pullback
statement: Let $u:V\to U$ be a surjective morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism] of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then $F$ is constructible if and only if $u^{-1}F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: Use the comparison of finite-constant-value constructibility with IsConstructibleSheaf, and the proved arbitrary-morphism preservation IsConstructibleSheaf.upperStar, to obtain the forward implication and preservation for every constructible presentation object.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: For any H whose pullback is constructible, choose its filtered colimit presentation by constructible module sheaves. The coefficient-category inverse image Etale.upperStar is a left adjoint, so the mapped cocone is colimiting. Constructible-source factorization applied to the identity on its pullback gives a split epimorphic pulled-back colimit leg.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: Surjectivity makes module pullback faithful by the existing geometric-stalk theorem. A faithful functor reflects epimorphisms, so the selected colimit leg itself is epi. Thus every H with constructible pullback admits an epimorphism from a constructible module sheaf.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: Apply the quotient-presentation argument first to F to obtain p:G→F. Pullback preserves kernels, and the two pulled-back sheaves are constructible, so the kernel clause of the constructible Serre theorem shows that the pullback of ker(p) is constructible. Apply the same quotient-presentation argument to ker(p), obtaining r:C→ker(p) epi with C constructible.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: The cokernel of r followed by the kernel inclusion is isomorphic to the cokernel of that inclusion because r is epi. Since p is epi in the abelian category of module sheaves, the latter cokernel is F. The constructible cokernel clause and invariance under isomorphism therefore show F is constructible; compare back to finite constant values.
